name: Tiny Mode
author: the loader's own repo
description: Shrinks the player and slows its movement by the same factor, so the world reads as giant. Set the size with the in-launcher slider (0.10x to 0.50x, default 0.5x); half size means half speed. Deleting the mod is the only off.

fields.label: Player scale
fields.help: The player's size, and its walk speed scaled by the same factor. 0.5 = half size, half speed. The slider stops at 0.50 because that is the supported range; hand-edit tiny-mode.json to go smaller than 0.10 or larger than 0.50 and the mod will honor it. Movement and speed are only adjusted once you are inside a map.

_note: The launcher writes the slider value to configPath (a %LOCALAPPDATA% sidecar); the mod reads scale from there first, then falls back to the top-level 'scale' in this file, then 0.5. Beyond-slider values survive - the mod clamps only to a sanity window (0.05..4.0), never to the slider bounds. Speed is not a separate knob: it is the game's own base move speed times the chosen scale. Live memory tracing plus disassembly of PlayerBehaviour.HandleMovement proved the mover computes speed from PlayerBehaviour.moveSpeed at +0xF0 (harvested offset 240), which is NOT a float but a CompoundFloat (Eternity.Utility.CompoundValues) holding BaseValue at +0x10 (get_BaseValue is movss xmm0,[rcx+10h]) and the recomputed Value cache at +0x48 (get_Value is movss xmm0,[rcx+48h]). The mod reads that object off the player it already captures and, every beat, writes base*scale to BaseValue (+0x10) AND to the Value cache (+0x48): the mover multiplies by the cache, and the game recomputes it event-driven (map load, sprint bonus add/remove), so a conditional mirror loses that race and walking silently returns to full speed. The cost is that game-side speed bonuses are over-asserted while the mod is on; half size = half speed always holds. Verified live: holding the cache at 0.5 made a 3s walk cross ~1.5 m where full speed crosses a whole zone. The earlier theory (PlayerBehaviourSettings.moveSpeed at +0x24, reached via the get_MoveSpeed receiver or gameSettings +0xC0) was disproved live - poking those left walking at full speed; the 'static' path in HandleMovement is Vector3's class statics. gameBuild records the build this was harvested and verified against (26611978); methods are still resolved by identity at runtime, so nothing here is a baked token.
